newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes at year-high vs US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes at year-high vs US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan ended up against the U.S. dollar on Monday in Shanghai at its highest closing level since August 14 last year due to strong pro-yuan sentiment sparked by China's growing foreign trade surplus, traders said.
The local currency ended up at 8.3048 from last Friday's 8.3052 against the dollar on the Shanghai-based interbank foreign exchange market.
The previous higher closing rate of 8.3035 was set on August 14 last year.
Local media reported on Saturday that China posted a trade surplus of $2.99 billion in August, bringing the surplus in the first eight months of this year to $4.99 billion.
Dealers said the news prompted strong bids for the yuan today and pushed it to close above the main 8.3050 resistance level.

"The yuan breached the main resistance level today after weeks of consolidation due to the news of the trade surplus," said one trader. "Many traders expect the yuan to continue to rise due to a surplus of the dollar on the market, with China's foreign trade position growing stronger."
"The yuan is widely expected to continue rising in the short term," a second dealer said. "But it is likely to go up slowly because of expected central bank intervention."
The People's Bank of China has intervened to depress the yuan since the market was established in 1994, to stabilise the local currency.
In today's trading, the yuan opened slightly up at 8.3051.
After hitting an intra-day low of 8.3053 early in the session, it rose above the 8.3050 level and consolidated in a range of 8.3046-8.3048 for most of the session.
It hit a high of 8.3040 about 15 minutes before closing.
Trading was more active than last Friday, with most done at about 8.3047, traders said.
Dealers said the yuan would move around 8.3050 on Tuesday.
The yuan closed up at an intra-day high of 7.5030 from 7.5250 against 100 Japanese yen and also at an intra-day high of 1.0732, up from 1.0737 against the Hong Kong dollar.
